extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: A massive multi-discipline multimodal understanding and reasoning benchmark with 11.5K college-level multimodal questions across six disciplines, 30 subjects, and 183 subfields.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was curated in three stages: selecting subjects based on common use of visual inputs, recruiting over 50 university students including co-authors to collect multimodal questions from textbooks and online resources and create new questions when necessary, and applying quality control including duplicate detection, format and typo checking, and difficulty filtering.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Document analysis, Others
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: College exams, quizzes, textbooks, online sources, and lecture materials.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data cleaning included identifying potential duplicates using lexical overlap and source URL similarity, author review to remove duplicates, format and typo checking, and excluding approximately 10% of problems classified as very easy.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, collected multimodal questions from textbooks and online resources and created new questions when necessary; authors then categorized problems into four difficulty levels.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Authors reviewed suspected duplicates, checked formatting and typos, and categorized problems into four difficulty levels, excluding about 10% that were too easy.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the selected majors; 90 college senior students were involved as human experts for evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: A version change log is included in the supplementary material.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is motivated by the societal importance of monitoring progress toward Expert AGI because such systems could substitute for skilled adult labor and lead to job displacement and economic disruption.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark may carry biases from manual curation, focuses only on college-level subjects, is not sufficient by itself to test Expert AGI, and lacks a direct mapping to the 90th percentile of skilled adults.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating multimodal models on zero-shot multimodal understanding and reasoning; includes few-shot development, validation for hyperparameter selection, and test splits.

name.evidence: We introduce MMMU : a new benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning.

description.evidence: MMMU includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: Our benchmark collection takes three stages. Firstly, we go through the common university majors to decide what subjects should be included in our benchmark. In the second stage, we recruit over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in these majors as annotators to assist in question collection. They collect multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: The questions in our benchmark were manually collected by a team of 50 college students (including coauthors) from various disciplines and subjects, drawing from online sources, textbooks, and lecture materials.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: We introduce MMMU : a comprehensive benchmark designed for college-level multi-discipline multimodal understanding and reasoning. It features problems sourced from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks spanning six common disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: To further control the quality of our data, we perform two steps of data cleaning. In the first stage, lexical overlap and source URL similarity are employed to identify potential duplicate problems. These suspected duplicates were then reviewed by the authors to identify and eliminate any duplications.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: In the second stage, we recruit over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in these majors as annotators to assist in question collection. They collect multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: These suspected duplicates were then reviewed by the authors to identify and eliminate any duplications. In the third and final stage, the authors categorize the problems into four difficulty levels: very easy, easy, medium, and hard. Approximately 10% of the problems, classified as very easy and not aligning with our design criteria due to their simplistic nature, are excluded from the benchmark.

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: In the second stage, we recruit over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in these majors as annotators to assist in question collection.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: It denotes an AI system that reaches “at least 90th percentile of skilled adults” in a broad range of tasks, thus starting to achieve “the substitution threshold for machine intelligence in lieu of human labor” for many industries, leading to significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: MMMU , like any benchmark, has limitations despite its comprehensive nature. The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI [57].

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: We shall caution that MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI, as per the definition [57], because there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and “90th percentile of skilled adults,” nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: MMMU , constituting 11.5K questions, is divided into a few-shot development set, a validation set, and a test set. The few-shot development set includes 5 questions per subject, and the validation set, useful for hyperparameter selection, contains approximately 900 questions, while the test set comprises 10.5K questions.
